questions.question: Why is Import Mode typically faster than Direct Query for interactive dashboards?
options: Import mode uses a faster internet connection
Data is stored in the BI tool's compressed, in-memory columnar engine, so clicks don't wait on network round-trips to the source database
Direct Query deletes old data automatically
Import mode skips data validation
questions.explanation: Import-mode engines (e.g., VertiPaq, Hyper) pre-compress and cache data in RAM, enabling sub-second slicing. Direct Query sends a fresh SQL query to the source on every interaction, so it inherits the source database's latency.

questions.question: In the BrightCart RLS lab, a user logs in whose email is NOT present in dim_user_role. What should a well-designed RLS rule do?
options: Show all rows, since the user is probably an admin
Throw an unrecoverable error and crash the report
Show zero rows, because the lookup returns blank and the filter matches nothing — a fail-closed design
Show a random sample of rows
questions.explanation: Good RLS design fails closed: if identity data can't be resolved to a role, the safest default is to show nothing, not everything. Failing open (defaulting to show-all on a missing match) is one of the most common and dangerous RLS misconfigurations.

questions.question: Why can a 'cached-data exposure' leak still occur even when RLS filters look correct in the report visuals?
options: RLS rules expire after 24 hours
If RLS is enforced only at the report/visual layer and not at the dataset level, anyone with direct dataset access can bypass the visual filter and see the full cached import
Cached data is always encrypted, so this can't happen
Direct Query mode is immune to this issue by definition
questions.explanation: Import-mode datasets hold a full cached copy of the data in the BI server's memory or disk. RLS must be enforced at the dataset/model level (not just the visual) so that dataset-level access (e.g., via API, export, or admin tools) still respects the same row filter.

questions.question: BrightCart needs to decide between Import and Direct Query for a flash-sale inventory dashboard with real-time stock counts. Using the weighted decision matrix, which factor should dominate the decision?
options: Data freshness requirement, weighted at 30%, strongly favors Direct Query for this use case
Source system load tolerance, because the warehouse is always idle
Governance needs, since RLS is irrelevant to inventory
Query complexity, because flash-sale dashboards always have complex queries
questions.explanation: The decision matrix weights freshness at 30%, the highest single factor. A flash-sale stock counter that must reflect live inventory scores high on freshness need, which pushes the weighted total toward Direct Query even if other factors (like interactivity) might favor Import.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of 'Headless BI' (a metrics layer) over defining the same metric separately in Tableau, Power BI, and a Python script?
options: It eliminates the need for any database
It guarantees prettier charts
It defines each metric once in code/YAML and serves it via API to every consuming tool, preventing inconsistent definitions across tools
It is always free
questions.explanation: Headless BI decouples metric logic from the visualization layer. Instead of redefining 'Net Revenue' in DAX, LookML, and a Python script (and risking drift), you define it once and every tool calls the same definition via API.

questions.question: Why does BrightCart's BI team use a dedicated service account (not a named employee's login) for scheduled refreshes and embedded reports?
options: Service accounts are required by Microsoft licensing terms
So refreshes and embeds keep working — and stay auditable — even after the employee changes roles, goes on leave, or leaves the company
Service accounts are cheaper than named licenses
Service accounts automatically fix data quality issues
questions.explanation: Tying automated infrastructure to a personal login creates a single point of failure: disabling that account (e.g., on termination) silently breaks every dependent refresh. Service accounts decouple infrastructure reliability from individual employment status.

questions.question: BrightCart's warehouse load finishes at an unpredictable time each morning. What refresh orchestration pattern avoids refreshing the dashboard on top of incomplete data?
options: A fixed time-based trigger scheduled for 5:00 AM every day regardless of load status
An event-based trigger that fires the BI refresh only after the orchestrator emits a 'data ready' signal
Refreshing every 5 minutes continuously
Disabling refresh entirely and asking analysts to refresh manually
questions.explanation: Event-based triggers (refresh fires only when upstream ETL signals completion) are safer than time-based triggers, which can fire too early if the load runs long and leave the dashboard showing partially loaded data.

questions.question: An employee moves from managing the North region to a corporate analyst role, but six months later still has 'Manager_North' RLS access. What governance gap does this illustrate?
options: A semantic layer failure
Entitlement drift — access permissions no longer match the employee's actual role because no periodic access review caught the change
A Direct Query timeout
A licensing violation
questions.explanation: Entitlement drift occurs when role/group membership isn't updated as employees change jobs. RLS rules are only as trustworthy as the identity data feeding them, which is why quarterly entitlement audits are a standard governance control.
